author: The Lizard of Oz
text_post: I always thought there was something slightly uncanny about these composites. They give you a good idea of the different national types, but none of them is the face of an actual particular girl; and the eye, being a terribly attuned instrument, picks up on that. Because of the perfect symmetry that results from the averaging, many of these faces are very near to what a very pretty -- not beautiful, cute, or hot, but a conventionally pretty -- girl that embodies her national type would look like; but without being enlivened by the character and the subtle, barely perceptible asymmetries of an individual face, that nearness remains inert and unrealized, creating a vaguely disturbing effect. I don't like to look at these images for too long.
